newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes end up on ailing peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes end up on ailing peso.

text.p: Late speculation reined in earlier gains on Mexico's overnight Cetes, which ended up 25 basis points at 27.50 percent, traders said.
"Those who had held on to paper had their way again. Speculation was spawned by another run on the peso," said a trader.
Overnight Cetes rates soared to a high of 29 percent in early trade when the peso was mauled in early trade.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed at its weakest level since November 1995, at 7.9150/7.9250 per dollar.
"When dealers saw the peso how suddenly the peso stumbled, they preferred to sit on the sidelines instead of taking risk positions," said another trader.

Other traders noted that speculation was also due to Saturday's renewal of the Alliance for Economic Recovery (ARE), a three-way agreement on economic guidelines between government, business and labor leaders.
Causes for concern were mooted price and wage hikes and changes in tax breaks for industry, traders said.
Overnight rates on bank paper, meanwhile, closed up 60 basis points at 30.10 percent.
Total credit maturities for Monday were estimated at 4.979 billion pesos.
Traders said speculative onslaughts on the peso could lead to another round of rise in primary rates at next Tuesday's Cetes auction.
